newsitem.title: FINLAND: Turkey says EU rebuff could kill customs union.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says EU rebuff could kill customs union.

text.p: Turkey's fledgling customs union with the European Union would not survive EU rejection of the country's membership bid, Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller said on Friday.

"If the enlargement list is a list that excludes Turkey, I'm afraid that what will happen in the future is that the customs union cannot survive because it will be blocking all other non-members... and that will not be long-lasting," Ciller told a news conference in the Finnish capital.

She was visiting Finland at short notice ahead of a meeting this weekend in Apeldoorn in the Netherlands where EU foreign ministers will try to reassure her that they have not turned their backs on Turkey.
Turkey's envoy to the EU said on Wednesday that Ankara could opt out of the customs union, launched in January, if Turkey were not included in the EU's enlargement plans.

Finnish Foreign Minister Tarja Halonen, chairwoman of the Council of Europe's committee of ministers, said Ciller told her that Turkey was taking the necessary steps to improve human rights, a key obstacle to Turkey's EU candidacy.

"I will tell (the EU foreign ministers' meeting) that I got a very strong feeling that Ciller was trying very hard to convince me that they have the will and the ability to progress," Halonen said, adding that Turkey still had far to go.
"We see some obstacles, some very, very serious obstacles, and these are in my eyes especially in the human rights issues," she said.
Ciller implied that EU reservations about Moslem Turkey had a religous element.
"I'm afraid a new wall of Berlin will be built on religious grounds," Ciller said. "We don't want to be discriminated (against)."
She neither confirmed nor denied that NATO-member Turkey was prepared to veto the alliance's expansion as a weapon in order to pressure for EU membership.
"We are not against NATO enlargement but what we are against is specifying Turkey out (of the EU)," she said.
